question: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhaulagiri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dhaulagiri** is the seventh highest mountain in the world, with an elevation of 8,167 meters above sea level.
 
• It is located in the **Dhaulagiri mountain range of Nepal**, in the Himalayas, and does not fall within the boundaries of India.
 
• The mountain lies northwest of Pokhara, a major city in Nepal, and is part of the Annapurna Conservation Area.
 
• The name "Dhaulagiri" is derived from the Sanskrit words "Dhavala" (white) and "Giri" (mountain), meaning "White Mountain."
 
• This peak was first summited on **13 May 1960** by a Swiss-Austrian-Nepali expedition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Shikar:**

 
 
• It is the highest peak in the Aravalli Range, located in **Rajasthan, India**.
 
• The peak stands at an altitude of 1,722 meters above sea level and is known for its scenic beauty and the Guru Dattatreya temple.
 
 
 
• **Nanda Devi:**
 
 
• It is the second highest mountain in India, with an altitude of 7,816 meters.
 
• Located in Uttarakhand, it is part of the Garhwal Himalayas and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Mahendragiri:**
 
 
• It is a mountain peak located in the Eastern Ghats in **Odisha, India**.
 
• The peak is associated with mythological references from the Ramayana.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Peaks:**
 
 
• The Himalayan range extends across five countries: India, Nepal, Bhutan, China, and Pakistan.
 
• India’s prominent Himalayan peaks include Kanchenjunga, Nanda Devi, and Trisul.
